answer: Bonded identity with quadratic voting resists Sybils. Each agent locks real collateral for one identity and may vouch only for peers it has transacted with, forming a trellis of attestations whose reputation signal fades when idle. Voting weight is the square root of stake, so splitting funds across fake clones earns no extra influence yet still needs a bond per clone. To sway a vote an attacker must outlock honest agents and fabricate deal histories, a cost rising with each new clone. Even a bot that writes a sonnet pays that bond, so mass clones burn capital faster than they gain power.
